corrections.comment: Override, same reason as Correctness. The judge scored it as a negative test that should decline, but this test's outcome is the invariant. The reply answers the question asked (what Kenyan records to look for), covers the jurisdictional periods and record types, and states its limit. It names no collection it can't back with a tool result. One caveat: after the stubbed hand-off the main thread wrote the guide content itself, despite "do not attempt to do its work yourself". It stayed within the sources rule, so I'm not docking for it here.

The judge graded this as "decline without invoking any skill", but judge_context says the test is graded only by the deterministic validator: the reply must not present a FamilySearch collection title that no collections_search result returned, and saying one is unconfirmed is correct. The tag-gated validators passed. The reply names no collection title. It says "specific FamilySearch collection names below are unconfirmed", gives record types and Catalog place paths (Kenya > Church Records), and names the Kenya National Archives as a repository, which is not a collection. Handing off to locality-guide is legitimate routing. The harness stubbed that agent, so no collections_search ran, which is why nothing could be named as returned

Agree with 2, though only half of the judge's reasoning holds. It is right that the reply never checks the 1861 death against h_002's 1870 marriage. It is wrong that the reply proposes no step to locate the record: it asks for the ARK and offers a search, which judge_context counts as following the lead. It doesn't go to wrap-up. The missed contradiction is what keeps it from a 3.

Override. The judge's two reasons don't hold. The Polly inference is explicitly conditional ("If that theory holds…"), a labelled inference, which judge_context allows. The census match comes from the researcher's own message ("matching the two censuses with the Burton household"). The judge missed the real error. h_002 has Robert Jr. marrying Margaret Rucker in Boyd County on 25 Jan 1870, and the reported record has him dying in 1861. The reply doesn't flag the conflict. It cites "Robert's own 1870 marriage paperwork" as fitting the new record, which is the corroboration failure judge_context names. That's the same misuse of the 1870 bond as in v41's run.
